purpose: General Solo progression at comparable permanent investment, including the 400-coin Starting move upgrade. Grades consider legal move routes and player discussions; the selected record period supplies dated supporting evidence, not a grade formula. Earlier assessments are retained when partners leave a top-50 snapshot. No controlled playtests claimed.

picks.reason: Mewtwo remains one of our first picks. Players repeatedly recommend it, its Psychic moves receive the single-type bonus, and the captured weekly Solo board contains 6 Mewtwo records.
picks.watchFor: We'd pair Special damage with Nasty Plot, not Swords Dance. The new Psychic control moves give you options, but don't assume every slot attacks before you earn Bonds.

picks.reason: We keep Gengar in S for its Ghost/Poison plan and repeated player recommendations. The captured weekly Solo board has 3 Gengar records; poison or slow can set up stronger Hex hits.
picks.watchFor: We'd use Nasty Plot for Special damage. Poison and Hex need to share an active Bond group to keep firing together; merely owning both isn't the full setup.

picks.reason: Eternatus stays high on our list for Sludge and the expanded Poison/Dragon pool. Its HP and speed give you room to build around status and damage.
picks.watchFor: We keep it in A while the new routes settle. It doesn't receive the single-type bonus, and older complaints about giant collision size should not be carried over unchanged.

picks.reason: We rate Giratina as a strong A option for its HP and Ghost/Dragon choices. Dragon Breath can apply slow for Hex once you can keep the relevant attacks running together.
picks.watchFor: We would take a coherent damage route as well as defensive cards. Recorded survival supports trying it, but does not identify a confirmed best build or the rules used for each run.

picks.reason: We like Palkia's Special Water/Dragon options, with Aqua Ring for regeneration and Whirlpool or Dragon Breath for another way to manage enemies. Water Gun remains a useful default.
picks.watchFor: We keep it in A as a move-route recommendation. It has no entry in the current captured boards; that absence is not evidence that its legal Water/Dragon plan stopped working.

picks.reason: We like Tentacruel for a Water/Poison plan with Aqua Ring, poison and Whirlpool control. It appears in ten captured weekly Group records; those are team results, and the Solo board currently has no Tentacruel entry.
picks.watchFor: We'd secure healing and a workable main attack before chasing extra moves. Shell Bell is capped at 4 HP per second; poison isn't unlimited sustain.

picks.reason: We'd lean into Sludge first: it already uses Munkidori's 1.42 Special attack. Psychic moves give you another direction if the cards suit it.
picks.watchFor: Watch the 66 physical defense. When you change attacks, remember that the other moves in your slots aren't all firing alongside it.

picks.reason: Appletun is our slower Grass/Dragon alternative, with Vine Whip, new ranged Grass options and Dragon Dance for a Physical plan. Its 45:00 saved result is worth noting.
picks.watchFor: We wouldn't call it strongest from that result alone. Move early at speed 91, and don't mistake Grass Knot or an evolution name for guaranteed healing.

picks.reason: We put Slaking among our first picks for a Physical Normal plan. Its own-type bonus, active melee reduction and 138 HP support Tackle or Body Slam; the captured weekly Solo board includes a 45:00 result.
picks.watchFor: We would build a usable damage group before chasing more buffs. Normal has no super-effective matchups, and the saved result does not reveal its permanent upgrades or loadout.

picks.reason: Marshadow is one of our stronger melee choices. Karate Chop fits its 1.39 Physical attack, and speed 130 helps you choose when to get close.
picks.watchFor: Keep a way out after each approach. If you switch to Special Ghost damage, you're also switching to its lower attack factor.

picks.reason: We'd consider Zapdos when we want the Electric projectile start with Flying moves available as another option. Thunder Shock uses 1.39 Special attack.
picks.watchFor: Change how you move when you change attacks. Discharge needs you closer to enemies than Thunder Shock does.

picks.reason: Alakazam gets our vote if you're happy to trade safety for a strong ranged opening. Homing Confusion uses 1.44 Special attack, with speed 128 for repositioning.
picks.watchFor: Don't let the damage tempt you into standing still. Its 95 HP and 45 physical defense leave very little room for contact.

picks.reason: We like Jolteon for a mobile Electric start: Thunder Shock gives you piercing shots, and speed 133 helps keep a gap open.
picks.watchFor: We'd take the defensive weakness seriously. It has 99 HP and 60 physical defense, with less type variety than some alternatives.

picks.reason: Mew is our more balanced alternative to the fragile Psychic picks. You still open with Confusion, but have 115 HP and both defenses at 100.
picks.watchFor: Expect less damage from its 1.25 Special attack than Mewtwo's. Choose from the moves actually in its pool rather than planning around its main-game reputation.

picks.reason: We'd pick Espeon for a focused Special Psychic plan. Confusion homes in and uses its 1.42 Special attack from the start.
picks.watchFor: Protect the gap around you: 99 HP and 60 physical defense aren't much of a cushion. Psycho Cut uses its weaker Physical side.

picks.reason: Raikou makes our A tier as a balanced Electric option. Thunder Shock fits its stronger attack side, with speed 126 and 110 HP behind it.
picks.watchFor: Physical defense is the weaker side at 75. Choose between Thunderbolt and Discharge based on how close you want to play.

picks.reason: We'd build Tyranitar around Physical Rock damage first. Rock Throw fits 1.44 Physical attack, with 115 HP and strong defenses behind it.
picks.watchFor: Move early with speed 104. If you take a Dark move, check its attack category before spending on buffs.

picks.reason: We like Ho-Oh when Special hits are your main concern: 118 HP and 154 Special defense give you a substantial buffer, with Fire and Flying options.
picks.watchFor: Ember uses 1.31 Special attack, not the higher Physical factor. That huge Special defense doesn't apply to Physical hits.

picks.reason: Celebi appeals to us as a balanced Confusion starter with Grass options when you want a change of attack pattern.
picks.watchFor: Check the category before changing your buffs. Grass Knot is area damage; don't choose it expecting to recover HP.

picks.reason: We'd lean into Metal Claw on Metagross. Its 1.44 Physical attack and 130 physical defense support that opening, with Psychic moves available later.
picks.watchFor: Plan exits before you need them; speed 107 isn't especially high. Confusion uses its lower Special attack.

picks.reason: We like Groudon for a Physical Ground plan with Bonemerang, Magnitude or other area options. Ground attacks benefit from its single-type bonus.
picks.watchFor: Mud Shot is still the default and uses the lower Special factor. Buying Starting move can remove that mismatch; take the opening you intend to support.

picks.reason: We like Jirachi as a balanced Metal Claw starter. Active melee reduction sits alongside 115 HP and both defenses at 100.
picks.watchFor: Keep upgrading damage. Neither attack factor exceeds 1.25, so we'd avoid spending every choice on defense.

picks.reason: We'd consider Lucario if you want both a Physical melee route and a viable Special alternative. Karate Chop fits Physical attack; Aura Sphere uses 1.33 Special attack.
picks.watchFor: Choose your distance deliberately. With 102 HP and both defenses at 70, getting trapped still hurts despite melee reduction.

picks.reason: Magnezone is our sturdier Physical-defense option for a Special Electric start. Thunder Shock uses 1.42 Special attack, with 115 physical defense.
picks.watchFor: Speed 103 calls for early repositioning. Metal Claw may be available, but it uses the weaker Physical factor.

picks.reason: We'd use Dialga's Steel and Dragon choices to build around the attack side we want. Starting move lets you choose a Special opening to use its stronger factor.
picks.watchFor: Metal Claw remains the default, not a requirement after the unlock. We'd check the category of the chosen start before spending on attack buffs.

picks.reason: We like Manaphy's straightforward Water choices: Water Gun to start, slowing Bubble attacks and Aqua Ring if you want regeneration.
picks.watchFor: Its 1.25 Special attack trails Palkia's. We'd keep taking damage upgrades rather than expecting regeneration to carry the run.

picks.reason: Darkrai's rating should reflect the Starting move upgrade: we'd consider a Special Dark opening instead of judging every run by default Bite. Its own-type attacks now get the single-type bonus.
picks.watchFor: The complaint about its Bite opening is real, but comes from an older version. Choose a legal starting attack after buying the upgrade rather than treating that weakness as permanent.

picks.reason: Victini is one of our flexible Confusion starters. Fire adds burn and different attack patterns without a major defensive weak side in its base stats.
picks.watchFor: We'd stick with one main attack early. Taking a new move at every opportunity can leave the whole set short on levels.

picks.reason: We like Chandelure's own Fire/Ghost options for setting up Hex. Shadow Ball already uses a strong 1.50 Special factor at the start.
picks.watchFor: Apply burn before expecting the stronger Hex hits. With 97 HP and speed 112, leave yourself time to get out.

picks.reason: Thundurus gives us a fast Electric opening with Flying choices later. Thunder Shock lines up with its 1.39 Special attack and speed 125.
picks.watchFor: Don't drift into contact while picking cards. Its 70 physical defense makes repeated hits costly.

picks.reason: We'd start Reshiram around Dragon Rage, which already uses its 1.52 Special attack. Fire gives you another direction when the upgrades arrive.
picks.watchFor: Fire isn't your starting move. Keep weather and enemy types in mind when deciding which attack to use.

picks.reason: Keldeo is an easy pick for our ranged shortlist: Water Gun and Aura Sphere both use its stronger Special side, with Aqua Ring available too.
picks.watchFor: We'd think twice before switching to Karate Chop without a plan. It uses only 1.10 Physical attack.

picks.reason: We like Greninja for keeping a Water Gun gap open at speed 129. Water and Dark offer several ways to change your attack pattern later.
picks.watchFor: Avoid narrow escape routes. With defenses of 67 and 71, the cost of getting surrounded is high.

picks.reason: Hoopa makes our A tier on the strength of homing Confusion at 1.52 Special attack, with Ghost attacks available as alternatives.
picks.watchFor: Give yourself an exit before approaching a crowd. Speed 107 and 60 physical defense make late escapes risky.

picks.reason: We like Lunala if you want a homing Psychic start with more HP behind it. Its 132 HP and 1.45 Special attack are a useful combination.
picks.watchFor: We'd finish a promising main attack before chasing every Psychic and Ghost option. You don't get all their damage at once.

picks.reason: Xurkitree is our pick when Electric damage is the priority. Thunder Shock uses its 1.65 Special attack immediately.
picks.watchFor: We wouldn't choose it for safety alone. Speed 113 and both defenses at 71 still require careful movement.

picks.reason: We rate Blacephalon for its Special damage and Fire/Ghost choices. Ember uses 1.53 Special attack, and burn can help set up Hex later.
picks.watchFor: Treat it as a fragile attacker. With 94 HP and 53 physical defense, we'd keep space rather than trade hits.

picks.reason: We like Zeraora for the room speed 138 gives you around a Thunder Shock opening. Its 110 HP is useful, too.
picks.watchFor: Build for the move you're using. Thunder Shock takes the 1.26 Special factor, not its higher Physical factor.

picks.reason: We'd choose Sneasler for a fast Karate Chop plan. Speed 128 and 1.42 Physical attack fit that job, with Poison alternatives available.
picks.watchFor: Melee reduction helps, but 60 physical defense remains a weakness. Special attacks use only a 0.92 factor.

picks.reason: Skeledirge gets our A tier for a Fire opening backed by 117 HP and 100 physical defense, with Ghost options for later choices.
picks.watchFor: Start leaving a closing gap early at speed 106. If you choose Hex, make sure you have a way to apply status first.

picks.reason: We like Flutter Mane for fast ranged damage: Shadow Ball uses 1.44 Special attack, and speed 135 helps you keep moving.
picks.watchFor: Its 135 Special defense can hide a very different Physical weakness. With 95 HP and 55 physical defense, contact is dangerous.
picks.name: Flutter Mane

picks.reason: We'd build Iron Moth around its stronger Special side. Ember uses 1.47, with Fire and Poison options for status and different attack patterns.
picks.watchFor: Keep out of contact with that 60 physical defense. We'd upgrade a main attack before spreading levels across both types.
picks.name: Iron Moth

picks.reason: We rate Gholdengo for a planned Special Ghost/Steel route. The Starting move upgrade lets you begin with a legal attack that fits its stronger Special factor.
picks.watchFor: Without that unlock, Metal Claw still opens on only 1.03 Physical attack. We'd account for the actual save rather than assuming every player starts fully configured.

picks.reason: We like Iron Valiant's choice between Physical and Special routes. Both factors are useful, and speed 127 helps you reposition.
picks.watchFor: You start with Fairy Wind. Build for that until you actually change routes, and watch the lower Special defense of 60.
picks.name: Iron Valiant

picks.reason: We'd consider Venusaur for a Vine Whip start with Grass area attacks and Poison choices to build toward. Its 106 HP gives you something to work with.
picks.watchFor: We put it below the leading ranged starters because its damage factors are more modest. Pick a main route instead of taking every type option.

picks.reason: Charizard has plenty we'd want to build around: Ember uses 1.30 Special attack, with Fire and Flying attacks to choose from later.
picks.watchFor: Give the opening move some levels before branching out. We'd check attack categories rather than automatically stacking Physical buffs.

picks.reason: Raichu is a straightforward Electric choice if that's what you have unlocked. Thunder Shock gives piercing shots and familiar follow-up options.
picks.watchFor: At equal investment we'd lean toward Jolteon or Raikou. Raichu's 55 physical defense and 1.20 Special attack are the trade-off.

picks.reason: We'd start Nidoking with Sludge and then decide whether to stay with Special damage or move toward Physical Bonemerang.
picks.watchFor: Make that decision before taking attack buffs. Sludge uses 1.17 Special attack, not Nidoking's higher Physical factor.

picks.reason: Golduck gives us a simple Water plan: piercing Water Gun, slowing Bubble attacks and Aqua Ring for regeneration.
picks.watchFor: We'd choose the stronger Water alternatives at equal investment. Its 1.22 Special factor and moderate bulk keep it in B for us.

picks.reason: We'd build Hitmonlee around Karate Chop and its 1.36 Physical attack. Active melee reduction and 110 Special defense help justify getting close.
picks.watchFor: Be careful with contact: 92 HP and 53 physical defense are thin. Aura Sphere uses only 0.89 Special attack.

picks.reason: We like Crobat's speed 133 for repositioning. Sludge starts at range, with Flying moves available if you want another attack pattern.
picks.watchFor: The opening damage is the reason we keep it in B: Sludge uses only 1.08 Special attack.

picks.reason: Porygon2 is a reasonable Normal choice when you want fairly balanced defenses. Its 108 HP gives the opening some room.
picks.watchFor: We'd plan beyond Tackle, which uses 1.14 Physical attack rather than its stronger Special side. The typed move pool is narrow.

picks.reason: Blaziken offers Fire and Fighting routes with both attack factors above 1.30. We'd choose the attack style first, then support it with upgrades.
picks.watchFor: Ember doesn't grant melee reduction. Speed 112 and both defenses at 70 mean you still need to protect your opening.

picks.reason: We'd use Aggron's 180 physical defense to support Metal Claw and a Physical damage plan.
picks.watchFor: Don't mistake that number for protection against everything. Speed 99 and 60 Special defense are why we keep it below the more rounded picks.

picks.reason: Regirock is worth considering when Physical hits are your concern. Rock Throw starts on a 106-HP partner with 200 physical defense.
picks.watchFor: We'd plan escape routes early at speed 99. Its damage and narrower typed pool are the compromises.

picks.reason: We move Deoxys to A for a fast Special Psychic plan. Its single-type bonus and new homing or pushback options make its damage and speed easier to build around.
picks.watchFor: 92 HP still leaves less room for errors. Speed above 130 has reduced extra value during Judgment, so we'd also invest in damage control and survival.

picks.reason: We'd consider Infernape when you want Fire and Fighting choices without a huge gap between its attack factors. Speed 123 helps.
picks.watchFor: Its defenses are only 71 on both sides. If you switch into melee, change how you position as well as which buffs you take.

picks.reason: Rampardos moves into our A choices for Physical Rock damage. It benefits from the single-type bonus, and Rock Tomb adds a control option to its expanded pool.
picks.watchFor: We'd protect its slower turns at speed 102. Its Rock attacks still have matchups to work around; high damage isn't a reason to walk into marked zones.

picks.reason: Spiritomb gives us a ranged Shadow Ball start with both defenses at 108. Ghost and Dark leave a few directions open.
picks.watchFor: Move before you need to at speed 93. Its 92 HP isn't a large reserve, and Hex needs status on the target.

picks.reason: Gallade is a B pick we'd take with a Physical route in mind, using Psycho Cut or Fighting options rather than committing Special buffs to default Confusion.
picks.watchFor: Starting move can fix the opening mismatch. We'd still check what attacks are actually active together before choosing between damage, control and defense.

picks.reason: Whimsicott is worth a look if you want a faster Vine Whip option. Speed 127 helps you choose your distance, with Grass and Fairy choices later.
picks.watchFor: We'd prioritize damage early: its attack factors are only 1.07/1.12. Grass attacks here aren't a team-healing kit.

picks.reason: We'd start Archeops with a Physical Rock plan. Speed 124 and 1.47 Physical attack fit Rock Throw well.
picks.watchFor: Both defenses are 65, so we'd keep moving instead of trading hits. Its damage stats don't make it a safe default.

picks.reason: Cobalion gives us a fast Metal Claw option with 111 HP and 129 physical defense, plus active melee reduction.
picks.watchFor: Its damage factors are only 1.20 on both sides. We'd keep taking damage upgrades while watching the lower Special defense of 72.

picks.reason: We like Delphox's option to move from Ember into Psychic attacks. Its 1.33 Special factor supports either direction.
picks.watchFor: We'd choose one main attack early. Splitting upgrades across both types can leave you short on damage, and physical defense is only 72.

picks.reason: We move Kartana up for its Physical Grass/Steel choices, including Vine Whip and Metal Claw. The expanded pool gives you more ways to control space around a melee plan.
picks.watchFor: We wouldn't dismiss it just for 31 Special defense: the defense penalty is capped. Fire matchups and your positioning matter more than reading that number like a main-series stat.

picks.reason: We'd build Cinderace around Physical Fire damage such as Flame Charge or Flame Wheel. The single-type bonus and a selectable opening give that route a clearer start.
picks.watchFor: Default Ember uses only 1.06 Special attack. Buy the opening upgrade if changing routes; Physical buffs won't fix Ember on their own.

picks.reason: Toxtricity offers us a Special Electric start with Poison options later. Thunder Shock already uses its 1.33 factor.
picks.watchFor: Speed 110 and defenses of 70 make it less forgiving than the faster Electric picks. We'd leave extra room to turn away.

picks.reason: We like Dragapult's speed 138 for keeping clear space around Dragon Rage. Ghost gives you another route later.
picks.watchFor: Dragon Rage uses 1.25 Special attack, not its higher Physical factor. We'd choose upgrades for the attack actually on screen.

picks.reason: We'd consider Ceruledge for Physical Fire/Ghost choices such as Flame Charge or Shadow Sneak, with a matching opening after buying Starting move.
picks.watchFor: Default Ember uses its lower Special factor. The revised pool offers alternatives, but we wouldn't assume healing just from its main-game identity.

picks.reason: Tatsugiri gives us a Special Dragon start with useful Water choices later: piercing shots, slow and Aqua Ring.
picks.watchFor: We'd keep contact to a minimum with 101 HP and 60 physical defense. Plan around the moves here rather than a presumed Dondozo pairing.

picks.reason: Voltorb offers a mobile Electric start with piercing Thunder Shock, and now has Thunder Wave and bouncing Electro Ball as additional choices.
picks.watchFor: We'd choose another reviewed Electric partner at equal investment. Its lower damage and HP remain trade-offs even though the single-type bonus also benefits it.

picks.reason: Chansey belongs in B for us, not automatically at the bottom. Its 182 HP is meaningful under the softened defense rule, and Normal moves now get the single-type bonus.
picks.watchFor: We'd plan for damage first, potentially using a Special Normal opening after buying Starting move. Low attack still slows clearing; it isn't a team-healing kit.

picks.reason: Magcargo still offers Fire and Rock area/control choices, including the expanded Rock pool, if you want to make the slower approach work.
picks.watchFor: We'd take a faster option for general Solo progression. Speed 91 and awkward Water/Ground matchups are the larger concerns; high Physical defense alone won't solve them.

picks.reason: Charmander gives us a straightforward Ember opening with the single-type Fire bonus. We would focus that attack before adding another slot.
picks.watchFor: Its 88 HP leaves less room for a bad approach than the evolved Fire options. Keep moving through open lanes rather than treating the starter label as protection.

picks.reason: We like Blastoise for a steady Water route: Water Gun to start, Aqua Ring for recovery and Whirlpool when we need control.
picks.watchFor: It gives up clearing speed compared with stronger Special Water partners. Extra defense helps with damage taken, but does not replace an escape route.

picks.reason: Beedrill fits a Physical plan around Bug Bite or Poison Sting. We would use its speed to choose the approach, then improve the attack that is already working.
picks.watchFor: Its Poison and Bug pool includes many Special attacks that use a lower factor. Do not add Nasty Plot to a Physical plan just because poison is involved.

picks.reason: Sandslash makes more sense to us with a Physical Ground opening after Starting move is unlocked. Bulldoze or Bonemerang can use both its stronger attack and own-type bonus.
picks.watchFor: Default Mud Shot uses its weaker Special side. Physical defense does not cover every attack, and its Special defense is much less forgiving.

picks.reason: We would try Rapidash for mobile Fire runs, using Flame Wheel or Flame Charge for a Physical route once the opening is configurable.
picks.watchFor: Ember remains the default and is Special. Choose the attack first, then the matching buff; speed will not save a route through a closed gap.

picks.reason: Electrode offers a quick Electric opening with Thunder Shock, plus Thunder Wave when we need room to reposition. Its own-type damage bonus helps the modest Special factor.
picks.watchFor: Extra movement above 130 is softened during Judgment. Electro Ball also has a current projectile-count caveat, so we would not plan around an immediate extra shot.

picks.reason: For Marowak, we would unlock a Physical Ground opening and build around Bonemerang or Bulldoze. That avoids spending early cards on the weaker Mud Shot default.
picks.watchFor: Speed 97 makes late changes of direction costly. High Physical defense is useful, but it does not let us ignore warning markers or Special damage.

picks.reason: Weezing gives us a flexible Poison route: Sludge works as the default, while Poison Sting supports a Physical alternative. The single-type bonus applies to either damaging Poison choice.
picks.watchFor: We would commit to one category before taking attack buffs. Acid Spray's extra-shot description has a current limitation; the poison effect is a separate question.

picks.reason: Magikarp actually starts with Water Gun here and can learn the Water pool, including Aqua Ring. We would play it as a fragile ranged partner rather than assume it is stuck with Splash.
picks.watchFor: Its 79 HP and low attack factors make the opening much less forgiving. A saved result does not show the permanent investment behind it; stronger Water alternatives remain our first choice.

picks.reason: Ditto has the ordinary Normal move pool in this game. We would keep a simple Tackle or ranged Normal plan and use the own-type damage bonus.
picks.watchFor: Transform is not a card in this pool. Do not choose it expecting to copy a boss's moves or stats; the modest HP and attack factors still need careful positioning.

picks.reason: Eevee can make a simple Physical Normal run with Tackle and Swords Dance, with the single-type bonus supporting that route.
picks.watchFor: We would take a stronger Normal partner at equal investment. Its move list is not a promise of in-run species evolution or access to every Eevee evolution's elemental attacks.

picks.reason: Snorlax gives us a forgiving HP reserve for a Physical Normal route. Tackle or Body Slam fits its stronger attack, and both gain the own-type bonus.
picks.watchFor: We would move early at speed 91 instead of relying on HP to cross a packed lane. Aqua Ring is not in its pool, and a large health bar is not automatic recovery.

picks.reason: Pichu can use Thunder Shock and the single-type Electric bonus, with Thunder Wave as a control option. We would keep the damage plan narrow until the first evolution is ready.
picks.watchFor: Its 79 HP and low defenses give little room for contact. Electric attacks are Special in this pool, so its slightly higher Physical factor is not a reason to use Swords Dance for them.

picks.reason: Umbreon is a steadier Dark option for us: Bite or Night Slash fits its stronger Physical side, while the own-type bonus applies to both.
picks.watchFor: It trades damage for bulk. We would secure clearing power early and keep dodging; softened defense scaling means those high defense values are not near-invulnerability.

picks.reason: Mudkip has the full Water route, so Water Gun, Aqua Ring and a planned evolution can support a run. We would prioritize one dependable attack before filling slots.
picks.watchFor: Speed 95 makes a late escape harder, and Water Gun uses its lower Special factor. Having the same cards as stronger Water partners does not give it their starting damage.

picks.reason: Swampert gives us Water recovery options alongside Physical Ground attacks. With Starting move unlocked, we would consider Bulldoze or Bonemerang instead of forcing a Special opening.
picks.watchFor: Water Gun is still the default. It has two types and no single-type damage bonus, so check the actual category and spacing of the attack you choose.

picks.reason: Lotad can combine Water control with Grass attacks, but we would first build a ranged attack that keeps a path open and add Aqua Ring when it helps.
picks.watchFor: Speed 91 and 88 HP make this a demanding opening at equal investment. Grass Knot does not heal, and simply owning Water and Grass cards does not make them fire together.

picks.reason: Ludicolo gives us a Special Water or Grass plan with Aqua Ring and Whirlpool available. Water Gun is a usable start while we decide which cards to finish.
picks.watchFor: The dual typing does not receive the single-type bonus. We would avoid splitting early levels across too many alternatives, and would check Energy Ball's extra-shot caveat.

picks.reason: We like Gardevoir for a coherent Special opening: Confusion fits immediately, with Psychic control and Fairy alternatives when the cards justify another slot.
picks.watchFor: Its Physical defense is less forgiving than its Special defense. Mist Ball and Draining Kiss have projectile-count caveats, so we would not treat either first upgrade as two shots.

picks.reason: Swalot gives us a reasonable HP reserve and an even choice between Physical and Special Poison routes. Sludge works without changing the default opening.
picks.watchFor: We would still choose one damage category before taking buffs. Equal attack factors do not make every move equally useful, and its speed is only 101.

picks.reason: Cradily has both Rock area attacks and Grass alternatives. We would start with Rock Throw, then add a second route only when it solves a positioning problem.
picks.watchFor: At speed 96, committing to a chest or narrow lane needs care. Grass Knot is damage rather than recovery, and the newer bouncing shots have count limitations.

picks.reason: Snorunt starts with Ice Beam and can use the single-type bonus on Ice damage. We would finish a reliable ranged attack before chasing several Ice cards.
picks.watchFor: Its modest attack factors and 92 HP make stronger Ice alternatives easier at equal investment. Ice Shard's first extra-projectile upgrade is currently limited.

picks.reason: Walrein gives us Ice damage with Water recovery and control options. Ice Beam already uses its stronger Special attack, so the default is a sensible place to invest.
picks.watchFor: It gets no single-type bonus and has only moderate speed. Aqua Ring can help recovery, but staying in overlapping attacks will still overwhelm a healthy run.

picks.reason: Latias offers a Special Dragon opening with Psychic alternatives and enough movement to choose a safer angle. We would match Nasty Plot to that damage route.
picks.watchFor: Dragon Dance boosts Physical attack here, not Dragon-type damage in general. Do not take it expecting to strengthen Dragon Rage or Special Psychic attacks.

picks.reason: Latios gives us a strong Special Dragon opening and a useful Psychic pool. We would improve one main attack before linking in a second source of damage.
picks.watchFor: Its access to Dragon Dance does not make that buff fit a Special plan. Mist Ball has an extra-shot limitation, and the board does not reveal the winning loadout.

picks.reason: Kyogre gives us a clear Special Water route from Water Gun, with the single-type bonus, Aqua Ring and Whirlpool all supporting that direction.
picks.watchFor: We would keep an escape lane even with the high Special defense. The records do not identify held items or permanent upgrades, so they do not prove one best Kyogre build.

picks.reason: Rayquaza lets us choose a Physical or Special Dragon/Flying plan without a weaker attack side. We would commit to the attack behavior we can position reliably.
picks.watchFor: Equal attack factors do not make both buffs useful for one move. Dragon Dance helps a Physical route; Nasty Plot helps a Special route. Neither is a team-wide buff.

picks.reason: Chimchar gives us an Ember opening with the single-type Fire bonus and access to ranged or moving Fire attacks. We would focus an early evolution before experimenting.
picks.watchFor: It is a Fire partner here, not the Fire/Fighting version of its evolution. Karate Chop is not in this pool, and its 90 HP calls for a clear escape route.

picks.reason: Roserade becomes more attractive once we choose a Special opening such as Sludge. Its Grass/Poison pool then gives us damage and status options that fit the stronger side.
picks.watchFor: Default Vine Whip is Physical and uses a lower factor. We would not choose Grass Knot for healing or assume Energy Ball's first extra-shot upgrade works as written.

picks.reason: We would use Garchomp for a Physical Dragon or Ground route after configuring the opening. Dragon Claw, Bulldoze and Bonemerang give several legal directions to build around.
picks.watchFor: Default Dragon Rage is Special and uses the lower factor. Being able to learn both categories is not a reason to spend on both attack buffs before the main route works.

picks.reason: Toxicroak gives us Physical Poison/Fighting options, including Poison Sting and Karate Chop. We would consider one of those openings once Starting move is available.
picks.watchFor: Sludge is the default and is Special. Neither defense is a large safety margin, so avoid treating a melee reduction as permission to stay in contact.

picks.reason: Mamoswine makes a strong case for a Physical Ground route with Bulldoze or Bonemerang. Its HP gives us some room to get that plan established.
picks.watchFor: Default Ice Beam uses the weaker Special side. Ice Shard fits the stronger factor but has a current count caveat; its first upgrade does not immediately add another shot.

picks.reason: With a Special Normal opening such as Hyper Voice, Porygon-Z can use its stronger attack, Nasty Plot and the single-type bonus in one coherent plan.
picks.watchFor: Tackle remains the default until we configure the opening. We would not assume a ranged attack solves every crowd, and Normal damage has no super-effective matchups.

picks.reason: Froslass gives us a quick Ice/Ghost alternative with equal attack factors. Ice Beam works as a start, while Shadow Ball or control can provide another way to handle a crowd.
picks.watchFor: Equal factors still require a category-specific buff for each move. We would keep a reliable attack while checking the Ice Shard and Shadow Sneak upgrade limitations.

picks.reason: Arceus gives us balanced attack options, a fast Normal opening and the single-type bonus. We would choose a Physical or Special route rather than fill slots with buffs.
picks.watchFor: The playable partner is not the invulnerable Judgment boss. Its Normal move pool does not grant every elemental attack, and high defenses do not make warning markers safe.

picks.reason: Excadrill suits a Physical Ground/Steel route after we change the opening. Bulldoze, Metal Claw or Meteor Mash can use its stronger attack instead of the Mud Shot default.
picks.watchFor: Its lower defenses make a late retreat risky. We would build around one workable attack rather than assume a high Physical factor makes every close-range option safe.

picks.reason: Vanilluxe gives us a Special Ice route with the single-type bonus. Ice Beam is a usable default, and Powder Snow or Freeze-Dry can give a different attack pattern.
picks.watchFor: We would prioritize consistent coverage over another similar attack. Ice Shard uses the lower Physical factor and its first extra-shot upgrade has a current limitation.

picks.reason: Cryogonal gives us a mobile Special Ice route with Ice Beam and the own-type bonus. Its movement helps us choose an angle before firing into a crowd.
picks.watchFor: Physical defense is only 50, so high Special defense does not make contact safe. We would keep the Ice Shard count caveat in mind before switching to a Physical attack.

picks.reason: Durant fits a mobile Physical Bug/Steel route with Bug Bite or Metal Claw. We would improve the opening attack before adding Meteor Mash or another alternative.
picks.watchFor: Its Special defense is much lower than its Physical defense. Signal Beam and Mirror Shot use the weaker Special side and have current extra-shot limitations.

picks.reason: Volcarona benefits from a Special opening after Starting move is unlocked. Ember, Fire Spin or Bug Buzz gives us a route that fits its stronger attack.
picks.watchFor: Bug Bite is the Physical default, so the opening upgrade matters. We would not carry main-series ability assumptions into this game or use Swords Dance for Special Fire damage.

picks.reason: Kyurem gives us a substantial HP reserve and equal attack factors for Dragon or Ice. We would choose the attack pattern first and build its matching evolution.
picks.watchFor: It gets no single-type bonus. Dragon Dance helps Physical attacks only, and Ice Shard's first extra-projectile upgrade currently leaves one shot.

picks.reason: Clawitzer gives us a straightforward Special Water route with Water Gun, the own-type bonus and Aqua Ring available for recovery.
picks.watchFor: At speed 103, we would leave a closing lane early. The move pool does not prove a special main-series ability is active; judge the attacks and modifiers actually listed here.

picks.reason: Sylveon gives us Special Fairy damage with the single-type bonus. Fairy Wind or Dazzling Gleam can anchor the run while we consider control or recovery.
picks.watchFor: Draining Kiss has a real drain field, but its first extra-shot upgrade is limited. We would not infer unlimited recovery from the move name or replace every damage upgrade with healing.

picks.reason: Diancie offers Rock and Fairy alternatives with equal attack factors. We would keep Rock Throw as a workable start and add another pattern when the run needs it.
picks.watchFor: Its high defenses are softened by the game's damage formula, while HP and speed are modest. Power Gem and Draining Kiss also have current extra-shot caveats.

picks.reason: Primarina gives us a strong Special Water opening, Aqua Ring and Fairy alternatives. We would finish the main Water attack before making the second type a separate project.
picks.watchFor: It gets no single-type bonus. Draining Kiss's first projectile-count upgrade is limited, and Play Rough uses the lower Physical factor.

picks.reason: Toxapex gives us Water recovery and Poison options in the same pool. We would establish Sludge or a configured Water attack before building a defensive plan around it.
picks.watchFor: Its defenses do not cancel out speed 93 and modest damage. The playable partner does not automatically heal teammates; each player manages their own attack and buffs.

picks.reason: Palossand starts with a Special Shadow Ball route and can add Ground control or a slow setup for Hex. We would keep the main attack working before adding another slot.
picks.watchFor: Speed 93 leaves little room for a late escape. Shadow Sneak is Physical and has a count caveat, so it is not an automatic upgrade over the Special opening.

picks.reason: Nihilego becomes a more coherent pick with a Special opening such as Sludge. Its Poison and Special Rock options then use the stronger attack factor.
picks.watchFor: Rock Throw is the Physical default and uses a much lower factor. Its Physical defense is also low, and Power Gem's extra-shot upgrade is currently limited.

picks.reason: Buzzwole fits a Physical Bug/Fighting plan from the Bug Bite opening. Karate Chop or a moving Physical attack can add another pattern when the cards support it.
picks.watchFor: Special defense is much lower than Physical defense. Aura Sphere is legal but uses a lower attack factor, and extra melee reduction is not full protection.

picks.reason: Pheromosa gives us fast Bug/Fighting options with equal attack factors. We would choose a main attack whose range we can manage and build the matching buff around it.
picks.watchFor: Both defenses are low. Extra speed above 130 is softened in Judgment, so we would not trade away every damage or survival upgrade for more movement.

picks.reason: Naganadel gives us a Special Sludge opening with Dragon alternatives and good movement. Poison or a slow setup can support a coherent damage group once Bonds arrive.
picks.watchFor: Dragon Dance does not buff its Special attacks. We would not add every attractive move before the main attack can handle the next crowd.

picks.reason: Stakataka gives us a hard-hitting Physical Rock opening and Steel alternatives. We would use that damage to keep lanes clear rather than plan to absorb every attack.
picks.watchFor: Speed 83 is a serious positioning constraint. Its extreme Physical defense still uses the softened formula, and Power Gem or Mirror Shot uses the weaker Special side.

picks.reason: Polteageist gives us a Special Shadow Ball opening with the single-type Ghost bonus. Nasty Plot fits that direction, and Hex becomes an option when we can supply status.
picks.watchFor: Its own Ghost pool does not automatically supply every poison or burn setup. We would check the source of status before treating Hex as permanently empowered.

picks.reason: Regieleki gives us a very mobile Electric route with the own-type bonus and Thunder Wave for control. Thunder Shock is a usable opening without extra configuration.
picks.watchFor: Judgment softens movement above 130; speed 162 is not an uncapped escape advantage. Electro Ball also has a count limitation, so we would keep a dependable main attack.

picks.reason: Spectrier gives us a fast Special Shadow Ball opening with the single-type Ghost bonus. We would take Nasty Plot for that route and add control only when needed.
picks.watchFor: Physical defense is only 60, so we would not use speed as a substitute for reading warning markers. Hex needs a real status setup rather than a name-based damage assumption.

picks.reason: Sprigatito starts with Physical Razor Leaf, which fits its stronger side and the single-type Grass bonus. We would keep that route focused before adding another attack.
picks.watchFor: Its 88 HP leaves less margin than stronger Grass partners. Energy Ball is Special and has a current extra-shot caveat, while Grass Knot is not a healing move.

picks.reason: Meowscarada gives us a fast Physical Grass/Dark route from Vine Whip. Bite, Night Slash or another legal Physical option can give a different way to approach a crowd.
picks.watchFor: It receives no single-type bonus. Sucker Punch has a count caveat, so we would judge the upgrade by its actual shots rather than assume immediate extra coverage.

picks.reason: Glimmora makes more sense to us with Special Sludge or a Special Rock opening after configuration. That uses its stronger factor while retaining Poison and Rock alternatives.
picks.watchFor: Default Rock Throw is Physical. Power Gem and Acid Spray have count limitations, so we would avoid planning the opening around an extra shot that does not appear.

picks.reason: Baxcalibur suits a Physical Dragon route with Dragon Claw or Outrage after configuring the opening. Its HP helps us establish that plan before adding a second attack.
picks.watchFor: Dragon Rage is the Special default and uses a lower factor. Ice Shard fits Physical attack but its first extra-projectile upgrade is currently limited.

picks.reason: Roaring Moon suits a mobile Physical Dragon/Dark route once the opening is configured. We would choose Dragon Claw or Bite before spending on a matching Physical buff.
picks.watchFor: Default Dragon Rage uses only its lower Special factor. Sucker Punch's first extra-shot upgrade is limited, and extra move slots still do not all cast together.
picks.name: Roaring Moon

picks.reason: Koraidon fits a Physical Fighting route immediately through Karate Chop. Its Dragon options give us another attack pattern if the main attack and Bonds are ready.
picks.watchFor: Speed above 130 is softened during Judgment. Dragon Rage and Aura Sphere use the weaker Special factor, so neither is a free damage improvement over a Physical plan.
